title: OIG Report OIG-26-22: 'Alligator Alcatraz' Used Unprecedented Metal Cages, Multiple Violations
excerpt: A DHS OIG unannounced inspection of Florida's 'Alligator Alcatraz' soft-sided detention facility found that 79 detainees were confined in 18-square-foot metal enclosures — a practice the OIG called unprecedented among all ICE facilities it has ever inspected — along with widespread failures in medical care, food safety, and sanitation.
content:
On September 11, 2026, the DHS Office of Inspector General released Report OIG-26-22, the result of an unannounced January 21, 2026 inspection of the Florida Soft-Sided Facility (FSSF) in Ochopee, Florida — colloquially known as "Alligator Alcatraz." The report was delayed by approximately seven months due to a DHS OIG funding lapse from February 14 through April 30, 2026.

  • Between July 17, 2025, and January 18, 2026, the facility confined 79 detainees in small outdoor metal enclosures offering approximately 18 square feet of floor space, for periods ranging from several minutes to nearly two hours. The OIG stated this practice was
    "unprecedented among detention facilities OIG has inspected and presents significant risks to detainee health and safety."
  • Inspectors observed locking mechanisms on the enclosures, contradicting staff claims that detainees were never locked inside.
  • The facility failed to comply with standards for environmental health and safety, special management units, medical care, food service, personal hygiene, and recreation.
  • Freezers ran 10 to 14 degrees above safe temperature thresholds. Detainees were unable to wash their drinking cups. Showers were available only three times per week and were found to be infested with insects.
  • Facility leadership could not identify which detention standards applied. When asked, the warden and staff gave inconsistent answers. One official told inspectors it was "so gray as to whose place this is… and which standards to follow."
  • DHS responded by asserting that the State of Florida, which operated the site under 287(g) authority, bore responsibility for the violations. However, OIG noted all detainees were in ICE custody, ICE personnel were on site, and FEMA obligated $608.4 million to Florida for the facility.
  • The OIG issued 10 corrective recommendations, but all were administratively closed after the facility ceased operations on June 15, 2026, without remediation.

The OIG noted that questions surrounding federal oversight of state-run immigration detention remain pressing, as similar facilities continue to operate without scheduled federal oversight inspections.
